strategy_title: Fix B-Matrix Load Stride to Improve L2 Hit Rate
strategy_description: Rewriting the B-matrix load from a double-broadcast pattern (stride-96 along N) to direct pointer arithmetic with stride-1 along K (idx_k + 96*idx_n) improved the L2 hit rate from 50.3% to 69.57% and reduced elapsed cycles from 10548 to 10336, yielding a 1.04x speedup. The key causal change was correcting the memory access pattern so that consecutive threads access contiguous K-dimension elements, improving cache locality without changing occupancy, register pressure, or block/grid configuration. This approach is applicable whenever a GEMM kernel's inner-loop matrix load uses a strided broadcast pattern that causes poor cache reuse, identifiable by low L2 hit rate and SharedMemoryConflicts/CPIStall NCU rules.
slow_pseudocode:
# B load with double-broadcast, stride-96 along N (poor cache locality)
k_offs = offs_k[:, None] + k_idx * BLOCK_K   # [BLOCK_K, 1]
n_offs = offs_b_n[None, :]                    # [1, BLOCK_N]
b = tl.load(B + k_offs * 1 + n_offs * 96)    # stride-96 along N
fast_pseudocode:
# B load with direct pointer arithmetic, stride-1 along K (better cache locality)
idx_k = offs_k[:, None] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)  # [BLOCK_K, 1]
idx_n = offs_b_n[None, :]                     # [1, BLOCK_N]
b = tl.load(B + (idx_k + 96 * idx_n))         # stride-1 along K
applicable_when: GEMM kernel inner-loop B-matrix load uses a broadcast/strided pattern with large stride along the fast-varying dimension; L2 hit rate is below 60%; SharedMemoryConflicts and CPIStall NCU rules are triggered; block/grid configuration and register pressure are already at their optimal values.
do_not_apply_when: The B-matrix is already loaded with stride-1 along the contiguous dimension; or when changing the load pattern would alter the logical matrix indexing and break correctness (verify max_diff < atol before applying). Do not combine with tile-size changes, as prior attempts showed max_diff up to 31.8 when tile sizes were modified alongside the load rewrite.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.load with pointer arithmetic `B + (idx_k + stride * idx_n)` is equivalent to a 2D strided load. Ensure the stride constant (96 in this case) matches the actual leading dimension of the B matrix in memory. The double-broadcast pattern `tl.load(B + k_offs * stride_bk + n_offs * stride_bn)` is functionally equivalent but may generate different memory access patterns depending on how the compiler resolves the broadcast.
